MESSAGE


Dr. R.N. Jadli
President
All India Food Processors’ Association

On behalf of All India Food Processors’ Association (AIFPA), we heartily welcome all Exhibitors,
Visitors and Participants at the 39th AAHAR - The International Food and Hospitality Fair being held
from 4th – 8th March, 2025 at Bharat Mandapam, Pragati Maidan, New Delhi.

AIFPA, as an apex body dedicated to the growth and development of food processing industry in the
country, takes immense pleasure in associating with ITPO, the organizers of this special event, and
conveys its heartiest compliments to the entire ITPO Organizing Team for this wonderful achievement. It
is a matter of pride for us that ITPO has been conducting this event so successfully since many decades.

AAHAR has today earned the credentials of a landmark expo in the country and provides great
encouragement to the food industry, startups, entrepreneurs, food technologists, food machinery &
packaging manufacturers, exporters, distributors and a number of allied activities over the entire food value
chain.  This is a remarkable contribution to nation building. We wish AAHAR greater success in times to
come.

Food processing has often been clouded with misconceptions of the consumers that processed foods are
unhealthy, lower in nutrients, containing artificial ingredients and are of potential risks to human health.
However, this narrative disregard the crucial role which food processing industry is playing to ensure
safety, enhancing nutrition, reducing food waste, and addressing global food security. Despite these
benefits, misinformation is being spread through various social media platforms by the self-styled food
experts fueling the perception that processed foods are inherently unhealthy or "unnatural". Therefore, it
is essential to bring consumer awareness for dispelling these myths.

Keeping this critical issue in mind, AIFPA is organizing its 80th Annual Conference on “Negativity &
Myths About Food Processing: The Science Behind Safe and Healthy Food” & AIFPA Food Safety
Award 2024 Ceremony on 6th March, 2025 at MR-19, Bharat Mandapam, Pragati Maidan, New Delhi,
India, during the India’s leading exhibition AAHAR-2025. The conference will be attended by large number
of Industry leaders, Food manufacturers, Scientists and Senior government officials.

We take this opportunity to convey our best wishes to the Exhibitors, Visitors, and Speakers of the 39th
AAHAR-2025 so that their participation is useful & fruitful in the Nation Building.



Signature

Welcome Message for the 39th Edition of AAHAR
On behalf of ARCHII, it is my distinct pleasure to welcome you to the 39th
edition of the AAHAR Exhibition, a premier platform that continues to
redefine excellence in the Food & Hospitality Industry.
AAHAR has long been a catalyst for innovation, collaboration, and
business expansion, bringing together industry leaders, entrepreneurs,
and visionaries from across the globe. This esteemed exhibition serves
as a dynamic hub where new trends emerge, partnerships flourish, and
opportunities unfold.
At ARCHII, we remain committed to promoting such prestigious tradeshows,
ensuring that businesses can showcase their diverse offerings while staying
ahead in this ever-evolving industry. AAHAR’s legacy of success stands
as a testament to the meticulous planning, dedication, and vision of the
India Trade Promotion Organization (ITPO), and we deeply appreciate their
unwavering efforts in making this event bigger and better each year.
As we step into another remarkable edition of AAHAR, let us seize this
opportunity to network, exchange knowledge, and embrace the future
of food and hospitality. I look forward to meaningful collaborations and
witnessing the continued growth of this vibrant industry.
Wishing everyone a successful and enriching experience at AAHAR 2025!
Rajat Pandhi
President, ARCHII

The Council of Indian Food Trade (CIFT) is an organization dedicated to
promoting and advancing the vision of "Make in India" in the food industry.
Its core objective is to elevate Indian food products both within India and
globally, establishing India as a leading global hub for food and agribusiness.
By fostering growth, facilitating trade, and advocating for the interests of
the Indian food industry, CIFT aims to ensure that Indian food products gain
recognition for their quality, diversity, and sustainability on the world stage.
CIFT’s efforts are focused on creating a vibrant ecosystem for the Indian food
sector that benefits all stakeholders across the value chain. This includes
manufacturers, exporters, farmers, food processors, and consumers.
With the ever-growing demand for diverse food products worldwide, CIFT
works towards strengthening India’s position as a competitive player in the
international market. By promoting innovation, encouraging the adoption
of responsible practices, and leveraging the latest technologies, CIFT is
committed to driving industry transformation and ensuring sustainability in
food production and trade.
One of the major upcoming milestones in CIFT’s journey is the participation
of its members in Aahar 2025. Aahar is one of the largest food and
hospitality exhibitions in India and serves as a platform for showcasing the
best of Indian food products, technologies, and innovations. CIFT's active
participation in Aahar is always expected to be a game-changer for the
"Make in India" vision. This platform will provide immense opportunities
for Indian food producers and exporters to engage with international
buyers, establish valuable business partnerships, and expand their market
presence. The exposure and networking opportunities offered at Aahar will
significantly amplify the reach of Indian food brands on the global stage,
promoting them to a wider audience.
At Aahar 2025, CIFT will also emphasize the importance of sustainability,
quality, and innovation, which are the pillars of the Indian food industry’s
future. By highlighting the diversity of Indian food products and the
expertise behind their production, CIFT aims to transform the perception
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

of Indian food on the international market, showcasing it as a symbol of
excellence. Through collaboration and showcasing India's food industry’s
capabilities, CIFT aims to align with global food trends and contribute to
India’s growing influence in global agribusiness.
Ultimately, CIFT’s vision is to ensure that the Indian food industry stands tall
on the world stage. With a focus on fostering growth, driving innovation,
and facilitating trade, CIFT is actively working to position India as a leader
in the global food industry, one that is recognized for its rich traditions,
commitment to quality, and sustainable practices. Through its collective
efforts, CIFT is paving the way for a resilient, prosperous, and globally
connected Indian food industry.
Board Members
Council of Indian Food Trade (CIFT)

Message
Leading FAIC into a Year of Innovation and Excellence
As I reflect on our journey, I am filled with immense pride and gratitude for our
remarkable strides together. I’m truly grateful to see how the FAIC community
has not only grown in numbers but also the quality of service, innovation, and
professionalism we bring to the hospitality industry. It’s your dedication and
unwavering commitment to excellence that continues to drive our success, and
I as President of FAIC, couldn’t be prouder to be part of this incredible journey
with you all.
As we step into an exciting new chapter, I am thrilled to announce the much-
awaited Aahar 2025, scheduled for March 4 – March 9, 2025, at Delhi Pragati
Maidan. This event will serve as a key platform for collaboration, learning, and
showcasing the best of our industry. It is an opportunity for us to come together,
celebrate our achievements, and explore new avenues of growth. Behind every
thriving business is a dedicated and motivated team. I encourage you to invest
in your people, reward their efforts, and provide them with the right tools and
training to adapt to evolving industry trends.
For the catering and hospitality industry to thrive, embracing innovation
is key. Tech-driven efficiency with AI-powered kitchen management and
smart inventory tracking will streamline operations. Sustainability will take
center stage, with a focus on zero-waste catering, eco-friendly packaging,
and locally sourced ingredients. To stay competitive, continuous upskilling
through online certifications and culinary training will be crucial. Personalized
customer experiences powered by data insights will help businesses tailor
menus to evolving tastes. Finally, cloud kitchens and virtual catering will offer
flexibility and scalability, adapting to the changing market. By adopting these
advancements, the industry can ensure lasting success.
With a fresh year ahead, let’s channel our energy into innovation, collaboration,
and raising industry standards. By uniting our expertise and passion, we can
redefine excellence in catering and solidify FAIC’s role as a leader in the evolving
hospitality sector. Together, let’s embrace new opportunities and set even
higher benchmarks for success.
Quote: “Confidence grows when a team trusts, learns, and succeeds together.”
Narendra Somani
President, FAIC

Dear Distinguished Industry Colleagues,
We extend our warmest greetings from the Forum of Indian Food
Importers (FIFI)!
We cordially invite all Food and Beverage (F&B) professionals to visit
Hall No. 1, the epitome of luxury and extravagance, boasting direct
access from Gate No. 6. This premier arena promises an unparalleled
experience.
We are thrilled to announce our strategic partnership with the
prestigious 'AAHAR' Food and Hospitality Trade show 2025, a flagship
event renowned for its pivotal role in shaping the agriculture, food, and
beverages industry in India.
Scheduled to take place at Pragati Maidan, New Delhi from March 04-
08, 2025, this esteemed trade fair is poised to be a ground-breaking
convergence of industry stakeholders, fostering meaningful connections
and collaborations.
As a respected industry leader, we invite you to join us at this illustrious
event, where you will have the opportunity to engage with an array of
esteemed exhibitors representing over 900 companies, 9100 brands,

and country pavilions from Brazil, UK, Canada, Thailand, Chile and
Australia.
FIFI has extended exclusive invitations to over 40,000 trade visitors from
across the Indian subcontinent, encompassing the entire spectrum of
the food and beverage industry, including organized retail, unorganized
retail, travel retail, e-commerce, hotels, restaurants, catering companies,
purchase managers, chefs, Government of India representatives,
diplomatic missions, international chambers, and numerous others.
We would be delighted to have your gracious participation and warmly
welcome you to be an integral part of this annual extravaganza, aptly
dubbed as AAHAR.

MESSAGE
The World Is Becoming Plant-Based – And India Can Lead the Way!
Dear Exhibitors & Visitors,
Greetings From Plant Based Foods Industry Association (PBFIA)!
As the world shifts towards healthier, more sustainable food choices, India
stands at a critical juncture. With rising concerns over food security, climate
change, and health, plant-based foods are no longer just an alternative
- they are a necessity. The demand for nutritious, cruelty-free, and
environmentally responsible food options is growing rapidly, and the Indian
market is poised to become a global leader in this transformation. But for
this industry to truly take off, we need a strong ecosystem that fosters
innovation, investment, and collaboration.
That’s where the Plant Based Foods Industry Association (PBFIA) comes
in. As the driving force behind the plant-based movement in India, PBFIA
is committed to creating an environment where Indian businesses can
thrive, our consumers can make informed choices, and policymakers can
shape a sustainable future. By bringing together key stakeholders around
the country, PBFIA is accelerating the growth of plant-based foods in India,
making it a mainstream and accessible option for all.
To further this mission, PBFIA is proud to present the 6th Mega Convention
– India Plant Based Foods Show 2025, a part of 39th AAHAR - The
International Food & Hospitality Fair, happening at Bharat Mandapam,
Pragati Maidan, New Delhi, on March 4, 2025. This landmark event kicks off a
pivotal moment in India’s plant-based revolution, uniting industry pioneers,
policymakers, investors, and food innovators to explore groundbreaking
ideas around Soy, infrastructure developments, interesting presentations
about protein clusters and tackle industry challenges to drive sustainable
change. Along with the main event, you  are also invited to attend the Plant
Based Foods Arena on 4th March, at Bharat Mandapam and Plant Based
Food Pavillion from 4th March to 8th March, 2025 at Pragati Maidan to
connect, learn, and be a part of history.
xxviii
And if you think plant-based food is just about salads and tofu, wait until you
experience the Plant-Based Foods Culinary Art Show at Culinary Art India
(CAI) 2025 6th March, 2025 at Hall No 5, Pragati Maidan! This exclusive
showcase will bring together top chefs, food scientists, and culinary experts
to demonstrate how plant-based innovation is redefining taste, texture, and
nutrition. From gourmet dishes to innovative plant-based alternatives, this
show will challenge everything you thought you knew about sustainable
eating.
So why should you attend? Because this is more than just an event -
it’s an opportunity. Network with industry leaders, discover the latest
innovations, gain insights from experts, and be a part of India’s sustainable
food movement. Whether you’re a business looking to scale, an investor
exploring new opportunities, or simply someone who believes in the future
of plant-based foods, this is where you need to be.
Welcome to the 6th Mega Convention – India Plant Based Foods Show
2025! Together, let’s shape our future  - one sustainable innovation at a
time.
“The future of food isn’t a trend. It’s a movement - and the time to join is
now.''
Best Wishes,
Praveer Srivastava
Executive Director

INDIA TRADE PROMOTION ORGANISATION
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
A PROFILE
The India Trade Promotion Organisation (ITPO) has a rich history that
spans several decades and has played a crucial role in facilitating global
trade and fostering economic cooperation among nations.
The first exhibition called “Railway Exhibition” was held at this venue on
April 16, 1953 to commemorate the hundred years of Indian Railways.
The exhibition complex took shape when the “World Agriculture Fair”
was hosted here in 1958. The Indian Industry Fair was a landmark event
at the venue during December 11, 1959 – March 8, 1960. Importantly,
this fair was visited by the then US, President H.E. Dwight D. Eisenhower
along with a high powered delegation. The exhibition complex was
rechristened as Pragati Maidan in 1972 when “Asia 72”, a mega trade
fair was held to celebrate the Silver Jubilee of India’s independence. The
venue again attracted global attention when Queen Elizabeth of Britain
visited Pragati Maidan in 1983. With the changing times and to meet the
emerging modern requirements, the venue underwent redevelopment
and named ‘Bharat Mandapam’ by the Hon’ble Prime Minister of India,
Shri Narender Modi on July 26, 2023.
India Trade Promotion Organisation (ITPO) came into being on January 1,
1992 with the merger of Trade Fair Authority of India (TFAI) established
on April 1, 1977 by an Act of Parliament and Trade Development
Authority (TDA) set up in 1970 as a registered society. The company is
registered under section 25 of the Company Act, 1956 (now section 8 of
the Companies Act 2013).
India Trade Promotion Organisation (ITPO), the premier trade promotion
enterprise of the Ministry of Commerce & Industry, Government of
India is committed to showcase excellence achieved by the country in
diverse fields especially trade and commerce. Its mission is to promote,
facilitate, encourage and coordinate various activities and programmes
to enhance India’s share of exports. ITPO provides a wide spectrum of
services to trade and industry and acts as a catalyst for growth of India’s
trade and commerce.
xxx
Significantly, grown with every business event in stature and dimension,
Bharat Mandapam, headquarter of the ITPO which is considered as a
symbol of the “Modern Fair Culture” in South-Asia region. ITPO manages
India’s world class exhibition complex which is constantly upgraded to
keep it in a high standard of readiness.
The primary objective of ITPO was to enhance India’s export potential
by organizing trade fairs, exhibitions and buyer-seller meets both within
the country and abroad. These events provided a platform for Indian
business to showcase their products and services to international buyers,
fostering business relationships and increasing export opportunities.
The history of ITPO is a testament to India’s commitment to fostering
international trade and economic cooperation. From its humble
beginnings as the Trade Development Authority to its transformation
into the India Trade Promotion Organization (ITPO) has played a pivotal
role in shaping India’s trade policies, promoting its products and services
worldwide, and positioning the country as a significant player in the
global market place.
The comprehensive revamp plan of Pragati Maidan (Now Bharat
Mandapam), IECC project was conceptualized by the ITPO as per
the direction of the Hon’ble Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi in
December 2015, the Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs approved
it in January 2017 for implementation in a mission mode. The project
has a total built-up area of 4.2 million sq.ft. comprising an iconic,
World Class Convention Centre that can accommodate 7,000 people
in a single format, six modern exhibition halls with an exhibition area
of 1.5 lakh sqm and plenty of underground parking facilities and good
infrastructure connectivity to encourage use of public transportation,
but also allow roads to decongest fast. The revamped venue Bharat
Mandapam is spread over 123 acres of prime land in the heart of India’s
capital, New Delhi.
The redevelopment of the venue was driven by the need to modernize
and expand the existing infrastructure, accommodate the increasing
demands of the trade and exhibition industry, and position India as a
global player in hosting world-class events.
ITPO’s regional offices are located at Chennai, Kolkata and Mumbai. The
Chennai Trade Centre managed by TNTPO is a joint venture of ITPO and
TIDCO in Chennai, Tamil Nadu and Trade Centre in Whitefield Bengaluru
xxxi
is a joint venture of ITPO and Karnataka Industrial Area Development
Board, managed by the Karnataka Trade Promotion Organsiation. Apart
from organizing several exhibitions such as India International Trade Fair,
AAHAR, India International Leather Fair (Chennai), India International
Security Expo, Delhi Book Fair and India International Footwear Fair,
ITPO holds national level participation in leading overseas trade shows
in line with the governments focus programmes for countries in Latin
America, Africa and CIS countries. Various policy matters were reviewed
and refined to promote third-party organizations at Bharat Mandapam.
ITPO has been strictly adhering to the CSR and sustainability guidelines
issued by the Department of Public Enterprises and applicable Act and
Rules of the Companies Act 2013.
Likewise, the formal commissioning of the Trade Centre Bengaluru (TCB)
at Whitefield in September 30, 2004 as a joint initiative of ITPO and the
Karnataka State Industrial Area Development Board, is the harbinger
of an added impetus to trade promotion through fairs, exhibitions and
associated activities of the State and southern region.
On the advice of the Department of Commerce, ITPO has coordinated the
construction of an exhibition-cum-trade-complex at Sarusajal, Guwahati
under “Assistance to States for Developing Export Infrastructure and
Allied Activities (ASIDE)’ Scheme. The Maniram Dewan Trade Centre
spread over an area of 10 acres has been completed and handed over to
Government of Assam for further operation. ITPO is providing assistance
to State Government of Jammu & Kashmir (J&K) in setting up Regional
Trade Promotion Centres (RTPC) in Pampore (Jammu & Kashmir).
Jammu & Kashmir Trade Promotion Organisation (JKTPO) incorporated
on 30th May 2018 as a Section 8 Company as per Companies Act, 2013
is a joint venture between Jammu & Kashmir Small Scale Industries
Development Corporation Ltd., (SICOP), India Trade Promotion
Organisation (ITPO) & Export Promotion Council for Handicrafts (EPCH)
with a proportion equity as 51% from SICOP, 44% from ITPO and 5%
from EPCH. An area of 270 kanals of land has been earmarked in an
upcoming area of Sempora, Pampore located just 8 kms from Srinagar.
Similarly, ITPO is also providing assistance to State Governments in
setting up Regional Trade Promotion Centres (RTPC) in Kochi (Kerala)
besides other state capitals and major cities.
At present ITPO owns and manages the Bharat Mandapam which is the
xxxii
largest exhibition centre in India both in terms of exhibition space and
the number of events held (approx. 90 events per year). The total area
of Bharat Mandapam is 123.51 acres (inclusive of 5.53 acres occupied
by National Science Centre and 2.49 acres by Crafts Museum.
xxxiii
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
BHARAT MANDAPAM
Bharat Mandapam has undergone a complete revamp to fulfil the
aspirations of the global exhibition fraternity. It promises to attract
global participants and business delegates from across the world with its
sheer magnificence, business conduciveness, architectural excellence,
and being a majestic landmark destination to be experienced in its
entire splendor.
To overcome the lack of modern amenities, absence of an integrated
exhibition complex and convention centre the Pragati Maidan 2.0 was
designed and International Exhibition-cum-Convention Centre (IECC)
was made a project of National Importance. The world-class Convention
Centre “Bharat Mandapam” was inaugurated by Shri Narendra Modi,
Hon’ble Prime Minister on July 26, 2023. Its establishment marks a
transformative milestone for India’s MICE Industry, opening up a plethora
of opportunities for both domestic and international stakeholders. This
ambitious revamp plan was aimed to position India as a crucial hub for
international activities while championing the spirit of AatmaNirbhar
Bharat.
The inception of the IECC Project traces back to December 2015 when
the government envisioned a comprehensive overhaul of the historic
Pragati Maidan in New Delhi. The Cabinet Committee on Economic
Affairs (CCEA) approved the proposal for the Integrated-Exhibition-cum-
Convention Centre at Pragati Maidan on January 24, 2017. The approval
marked a step forward in the realization of this monumental project.
In terms of capacity, the Bharat Mandapam provides a variety of spaces
catering to different needs such as general meeting rooms, premium
meeting rooms, G-20 room, Leaders Lounge, Auditoriums, special and
VIP. Level-3 boasts a grand seating capacity of 7,000 individuals with a
3000 seat plenary hall and a multifunction hall accommodating 4,000
attendees. A grand seating capacity of 7,000 individuals at level 3 of the
Convention Centre makes it one of the largest in the country.
Bharat Mandapam stands as a technological marvel, embracing cutting-
edge innovations to provide a seamless and state-of-the-art experience
for all its visitors.
xxxiv
Being a flag bearer of all that is Indian in the true sense, IECC celebrates
our country’s rich heritage by bowing down and paying homage to
our past and looking far into the promising future. The Iconic Bharat
Mandapam stands out as the project’s masterpiece, reflecting India’s
rich heritage while embracing the aspirations of a New India. It is
conceived with a unique architectural design that beautifully blends
India’s rich cultural fabric with the aspirations of New India.
Standing tall on a 6 meter high podium, the Bharat Mandapam reiterates
India’s vision of Growth and Development, a path that India is taking
towards becoming a Vishwa-Guru. Inspired from the Indian tradition,
the shape of the building is derived from the Shankha (conch shell),
the sound produced by which drives away evil spirits and is a mark of
auspicious beginnings.
One of the key highlights being a Pre-Function wall depicting Surya
Shakti, giving impetus to India’s continuous efforts towards green
energy through major milestones such as International Solar Alliance,
One Sun One World One Grid etc. Another Pre-Function wall depicts
India’s wheels of progress, our journey from Zero to ISRO, celebrating
our achievements in space exploration right from Aryabhatta to today’s
Chandrayan and Gaganyaan.
The G20 hall takes forward India’s ethos of Unity and Integrity and Global
Solidarity. Continuing the ideal of oneness, there’s also a typography
wall depicting the Pancha Mahabhuta-Universal Foundation, it signifies
the basic building blocks of universal foundation that are the five great
elements that equalize all of us. Aakash (Sky), Vayu(Air), Agni (Fire), Jal
(Water), Prithvi (Earth). All these symbols emphasize that the world is
one and reiterate the essence of India’s Presidency of G20 which rests
on the pillar of “VasudhaivaKutumbakam”. In addition to the symbolic
significance of these sculptures, the raw materials procured for their
fabrication are also by nature-Indian. These modest steps are re-igniting
the flames of a Self-Reliant India.
Also elements such as the Tree of Life and the India-Rising Sculpture
further articulate India’s free thinking, Progressive and Growth driven
mindset.
Apart from the architectural elements, there is also a myriad of colors
borrowed from the rich and diverse culture of India. From hand-crafted
Kashmiri carpets from the northern most part of India to the Tanjore
xxxv
Paintings from the vibrant lanes of South India. Bharat Mandapam is an
embodiment of India’s inheritance showcasing the spirit of “Ek Bharat
Shreshtha Bharat”. By inculcating art forms such as Kalamkari and
Madhubani Paintings, gives a wonderful peek into the folk history of our
country and at the same time giving these art forms a colossal platform
to further build “Brand India” by being “Vocal for Local”. Inclusion of
Tribal art forms such as Gond and Warli Paintings not only accentuate
the vision of an Inclusive India but also pushes forth India’s efforts of
tribal welfare.
Bharat Mandapam is not only an architectural marvel and holding
India’s cultural heritage in its heart, it also envisages a bright future for
the Indian dream of becoming the Light of Asia in the present century
by promoting Trade and Commerce, Enhancing small and Medium
Enterprises (SMEs), Attracting Foreign Direct Investment (FDI) and
creating employment opportunities.
Since its conceptualization, the Bharat Mandapam not only organized
one of the most prestigious international event G-20 but also met with
tremendous enthusiasm and interest from the market. Already, it has
received a staggering more than 100 enquiries for the next 24 months,
indicating the strong demand and recognition of its world-class facilities
and amenities. These requests span a diverse range of events, from
international conferences and ministry level gatherings to industry-
specific functions and sectoral conventions.
Bharat Mandapam epitomizes India’s pursuit of economic and
technological excellence. With its world-class infrastructure, it not only
contributes to India’s ambition of becoming a 5 trillion-dollar economy
soon but also reinforces the principles of Atmanirbhar Bharat. As India
sets its sights on the century of Asia, this centre becomes a beacon of
progress, fostering international collaboration and showcasing India’s
capabilities to the world. It embodies the spirit of Amritkaal, celebrating
the Azadi Ka Amrit Mahotsav, where India thrives as a global leader,
making its mark on the global stage and upholding the cherished
principle of “VasudhaivaKutumbakam” – the World is one family.
Bharat Mandapam is a landmark and iconic spot in Delhi and a symbol
of the Prime Minister’s vision of “New India” in sync with India aspiring
to be a global power. Fulfilling aspirations of expanding the business
fraternity, IECC will mainly cater go G2G, G2B and B2B activities. With
xxxvi
the latest architectural design along with basement parking for 4500
vehicles and comprehensive traffic decongestion interventions, it will
add to the grandeur, stature and profile of the capital city of Delhi.

AIFPA— INDIA’S PREMIER & PIONEER ASSOCIATION OF FOOD

AND FOOD INDUSTRY
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
VISION OF AIFPA
All India Food Processors’ Association (AIFPA) was established in the
year 1943 by some highly motivated and visionary processors mainly
involved in the processing of fruits and vegetables.
Subsequently, the Association took in its fold, processors from other
sectors of the food processing industry and now it has in its ambit the
food processors involved in processing of Fruits & Vegetables, Meat and
poultry, Fish, Milk & Milk products, Cereals and Pulses and
manufacture of a wide range of processed food products. These include
fruit juices and nectars, jams, jellies and marmalades, breads, buns,
biscuits and bakery products like cakes & related
confectionery items, various types of milk products and yoghurts,
ready-to- eat foods, confectionery items, various ethnic delicacies etc.
including other stake holders like food Associations, Plant & Machinery
manufacturers, Food Scientists/Technologists, service providers
etc. Member Industries account for a large percentage of the total
production of processed foods in India as well as that of total exports of
processed food products.
Since its inception, AIFPA had been significantly contributing to the
development and growth of the food processing in all sectors of agri-
horti commodities and thereby helping in reducing the enormous losses
of perishable commodities occurring in the country.
xl
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
MISSION OF AIFPA
The prime objectives of the Association include the following:-
a)	 To promote, encourage and support Indian Food Processing
Industries and raise the technical standards, product quality and
safety to not only meet the prescribed Indian Standards for safe food
as laid down by the FSSAI but and also to match global standards so
that Indian processed food products can have a good export market.
b)	 To actively participate in evolving quality standards & safety
measures under the Food Safety and Standards Act-2006.
c)	 To seek redressal of the problems of the food processing industry
that impede their growth and development by keeping a close liaison
and interaction with the Ministry of Food Processing Industries and
other Govt. agencies .
d)	 To conduct Workshops & Training Programmes to acquaint the persons
operating the food processing industry about GMP, GHP, HACCP
&FSMS Systems and also with new Technological Developments etc.
and also organise National/International Seminars.
e)	 To collect, classify and circulate statistics and other information
relating to production of agri-horti produce, production of processed
foods in India and agri-food exports from India.
f)	 To encourage research projects to study the technical problems of
the Industry and evolve methods of overcoming such problems.
g)	 To conduct and promote market research/market studies in India
and abroad to enable the growth of the Food Processing Industries
and help in the growth of marketing of processed food products.
h)	 To institute Awards and Scholarships to encourage Food Scientists
and Technologists to evolve and develop newer processed foods
which can widen and enlarge the market for processed foods.
i)	 To keep a good liaison with Govt. both with the Central & State
administrators, consultants and executives who can help in the
growth and development of the Food Processing Industries in India.
xli
j)	 To publish a bimonthly technical Journal under the name “Indian
Food Packer” which is over 72 years old and a monthly “E-Newsletter”
as non-profit activities, which aim to keep the food processing units
abreast of the latest worldwide developments in Food Processing,
new products & processes, food additives, research programmes,
food regulatory issues etc.
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
LIAISON WITH RESEARCH INSTITUTIONS
The Association maintains a close liaison with the Research Institutions
like the Central Food Technological Research Institute, Mysore;
Defence Food Research Laboratory, Mysore; Indian Agricultural
Research Institute, New Delhi, National Institute of Food Technology
& Entrepreneurs Management, Kundli, Sonipat, Indian Institute of
Crop Processing Technology, Thanjavur and other Institutes under the
Indian Council of Agricultural Research, Nutrition Research Laboratory,
Hyderabad under ICMR, Indian Institute of Packaging, Mumbai etc.
and refers the problems of the Industry wherever necessary to these
institutions for technological solution.
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
GOVERNMENT RECOGNITION
In regard to various matters concerning the Food Processing Industries
in India, the Association is duly recognized by the Government of India,
particularly the Ministry of Food Processing Industries as a Nodal Agency
and it has close interaction with various Govt. bodies, such as:
(i)
Union Ministry of Food Processing Industries.
(ii)
Union Ministry of Health & Family Welfare.
(iii)	 Food Safety and Standards Authority of India established under
Food Safety and Standards Act-2006.
(iv)	 Union Ministries of Finance, Agriculture, Commerce and Civil
Supplies.
(v)
National Horticulture Board (NHB), Ministry of Agriculture, Govt.
of India.
(vi)	 Agricultural and Processed Food Products Development Authority
(APEDA)
xlii
(vii)	 Export Inspection Council of the Ministry of Commerce, Govt. of
India.
(viii)	 Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS) & its various Sectional Committees
on subjects affecting the Food Processing Industry.
(ix)	 Empowered Committee of State Council of Finance Ministers on
Value Added Tax (VAT), GST, etc.
(x)
Quality Council of India etc.

SEMINARS & WORKSHOPS
AIFPA has been regularly organizing Seminars and Workshops at various
places in the country on topics concerning food processing, quality
standards of processed foods, new technologies in food processing, skill
development & technology up-gradation, matters relating to taxation of
processed foods, scope for marketing of processed foods both in India
and abroad etc.
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
INTERACTION WITH INTERNATIONAL ORGANISATIONS & EXHIBITIONS
AIFPA keeps a close liaison with Foreign Embassies, Trade bodies and
Chambers, delegations of different countries visiting India regarding
opportunities in the food processing sector for their investment and
development. Members are also encouraged to participate in the
International Exhibitions & Events concerning the food processing
sector.
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
MATTERS CONCERNING SAFETY AND STANDARDS OF VARIOUS
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
PROCESSED FOODS & LIAISON WITH FSSAI AND OTHER STATUTORY
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
BODIES
AIFPA has been working as a nodal body of food processors in regard to
the development of safety & standards for various types of processed
foods, holding discussions with stakeholders and suggest modifications
required before the standards are finalized and notified by FSSAI.
AIFPA is one of the members of the Food Safety and Standards Authority
of India (FSSAI) representing small scale food sector. AIFPA is also a
member on the Central Advisory Committee (CAC) of FSSAI representing
Food Processing Industry.
xliii
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
UNION FINANCE BUDGET
AIFPA has been making budgetary proposals every year on taxation
matters concerning Processed Food Industry and the products thereon
to the MoFPI for recommending them to the Union Ministry of Finance
for inclusion in the Union Budget.
AIFPA’S JOURNAL, “INDIAN FOOD PACKER” and “E-NEWSLETTER”
The Association publishes a bimonthly technical Journal titled, “Indian Food
Packer” (IFP). It is the official organ of the Association and is over 71 years
old. This Journal voices the views of the Association and publishes regularly
technical and other articles of interest to the Industry, Development News,
Industry News, Food Safety matters and food standards etc. It contains
nearly 100 pages of reading matter in each issue. Besides members of the
Association, the Journal has subscribers from Agricultural Universities,
Research Institutions, Home Science Colleges etc. in India and also a few
subscribers from foreign countries.
The Association is also bringing out a monthly E-Newsletter carrying
highlights & developments in Food Processing Industry/Food Technology,
Events etc. The E-Newsletter is sent widely to a few thousands mail IDs
of Food Processors, Food Scientists & Technologists, Food Machinery
manufacturers, Food Additive manufacturers and Suppliers etc.
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
AIFPA AWARDS
The Association gives Awards every year to selected Research Scientists and
other experts for contributing scientific papers of outstanding importance
and useful to the Food Processing Industry. It also gives awards to
distinguished personalities in different areas of Food Processing Industries.
AIFPA has instituted several Scholarships and Medals, which are being given
every year to selected students of Food Technology for excellence in their
courses.
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
MEMBERSHIP OF THE ASSOCIATION
The Association is committed to the growth and development of Food
Processing Industries in India and extends its active support for its scientific
advancement to meet the growing requirements of processed foods in the
Indian and export markets.
As on date, a very large number of members are on the rolls of the
Association and the Directory of Members contain all details about the
xliv
profile of each member’s corporate standing and can be accessed from our
Website:	www.aifpa.net
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
AIFPA GOAL
The sole aim and objective of the Association is to serve the overall
interests of its members and help in the growth and development of the
Food Processing Industries in India. While fully believing that in food sector,
consumer’s satisfaction & safety is of paramount importance.

AAHARTM –The International Food
& Hospitality Fair
Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi  (March 4-8, 2025)
AAHAR 2025 brief
The 39th edition of AAHAR - The International Food &
Hospitality Fair will be jointly organized by the Ministry
of Food Processing Industries (MoFPI) and India Trade
Promotion Organisation (ITPO) from March 4-8, 2025
at the iconic venue of Bharat Mandapam (New Delhi).
AAHAR is one of Asia’s best known brands in Food &
Hospitality shows.  AAHAR is one of Asia’s biggest B2B
best known brands in Food & Hospitality shows. The
show has a rich legacy of 38 years. The show has grown
by leaps & bounds in the recent years and has become
the ultimate destination for global vendors and sourcing
professionals. Spread over a gross area of over 1,10,000
sqm, AAHAR 2025 provides excellent opportunities
for Networking Avenues, Online Match-making, pre-
scheduled meetings and new Products Launches.
AAHAR is an order-writing show where the hotel industry,
restaurants, catering industry / institutions, importers,
buyers / distributors meet with vendors, to source best of
the products in the food, hospitality & equipment sectors.
Senior management, professionals like CEOs, Managing
Directors, Vice Presidents, Directors, General Managers
formed a substantial part of the visitors.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
ANIMALS
We strive for a world where everyone chooses
delicious and healthy food that is good for all humans, animals, and our planet.
ProVeg International is a food awareness organisation working to transform the global food sys-
tem by replacing 50% of animal products globally with plant-based and cultivated foods by 2040.
ProVeg has received the United Nations’ Momentum for Change Award and works closely with key
UN food and environment agencies. We have observer status with the UNFCCC and the IPCC, special
consultative status with ECOSOC, and are accredited for UNEA.
As a non-profit, ProVeg is philanthropy-driven. This is just one of many events we support all over the
world, in addition to the variety of work conducted in each ProVeg Country and through our ProVeg Grants
Program. Any donations are gratefully received and allow us to continue our impactful work.
